summary: A fictional scene from a novel's Book 10. Leon is offered a job in 'strategic research' by Brautigan, which is a polite reassignment away from the client work he has been doing. Realizing he holds the room's attention, he chooses to walk out instead of protesting or demanding more. He then meets a realtor who warns that he won't recover the roughly two million dollars he paid for his downtown loft near Broome and Grand Streets, since the market is falling.
one_line: Leon rejects a soft reassignment from Brautigan and walks out, then a realtor warns him his Lower East Side loft will sell for far less than he paid.
key_facts: Brautigan describes the new role as 'strategic research', involving figuring out what everyone is up to, putting people together, and proposing organizational structures.
Brautigan says the role uses Leon's talents, and when Leon raises the clients, Brautigan indicates Leon will no longer do client work.
Leon realizes he has the three people in the room in his power and could shout BOO! to make them fall off their chairs.
Leon chooses not to blow his top or ask for more; instead he says 'Nice working with ya' and walks out.
Leon says adios and buena suerte to Carmela on his way out.
The realtor is young, no-nonsense, black, and grew up on the Lower East Side, and advertises as 'A local realtor for a local neighborhood.'
Leon says he paid two million dollars for the place less than a year ago.
Leon's 80 percent mortgage was underwritten by Ate, who brought the interest rate down to less than two percent.
The apartment has a large corner picture window overlooking Broome Street and Grand Street.
The realtor says Leon will never get two million for the place in today's market and counts the FOR SALE signs in the neighborhood.
The realtor calls the buyers she does not want 'developers' and 'corporate apartment brokers' who rent by the week to VIPs.
The realtor says the slogans 'They're not making any more Manhattan' and 'Location location location' are lies.
The realtor says the market is designed to make buyers panic and spend more than they should.
